pages.lesson:
LESSON: EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.9: Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Extensive Reading helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading important?
2. How can we make reading interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a simple story and poem with appropriate speed for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
